diagnosis.strongest: HIER on the flagship pair - the delta fixed the board and its door in one treatment: no chip, a one-line ellipsised claim, READ muted and stated once above the table, and a door whose rows are chosen by recency and drawn at the board's own lead weight, none of it moving the changed feed off the top of home at either width or theme.

Round-1's critical is closed: the CLAIMED - UNVERIFIED chip is gone and nothing took its channel - no border, accent, underline or added rule weight appears on any board row, and the four rows carrying a real claim are now the only full-weight marks in that column.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Give /wiki/<entry> a number for its share of the 1440 shell and hold the template to it. The rest of what I carry is a capture setting (F-hier-9) and three hairlines (F-hier-11); this is the only place left where the widest viewport shows a reader no more than the narrowest does.

downstream.weakness: The board's cell problem is solved and the template around it is not: the flagship now sets a density standard - a repeated value stated once above the surface, muted on the rows, the exception at full weight - that the prose entry template has never been held to.
downstream.cause: Fixes 2 and 3 were written as invariants on named selectors on one surface, so they landed exactly; fix 4's invariant named .entry-rails, which this build calls .rails, and the implementer met that selector's clause honestly while the finding's own subject - the template's share of the shell - had no number attached to it.
downstream.recommendation: Before another round on the entry template, attach a share-of-shell number to R13 for measure-track templates so the next fix has something to falsify; drop the door's row rule with it, and re-capture /catalog at 390 as a viewport capture so the last open density question on this packet becomes answerable.
